## Orientation

Worktree only: `/home/andrewyin/se-workflow--red-first` (branch `phase/red-first`). Do not edit `.artifacts/`. Do not call adaptive-artifacts.

Territory: you own `skills/verify-work/SKILL.md` and any narrow skill-doc assert in `tests/test_assess_routing.py` (or similar). Do not change `scripts/close_batch.py` except if a skill example must match an already-shipped field name — prefer skill-only edits.

Base your docs on the request fields already enforced in close_batch: `red_check_run_id`, `red_result`, `red_revision`, `red_runner`, optional `red_diff_sha256`, plus green `check_run_id`/`result`/`revision` for tdd ancestry. Finding escape unchanged.

Commit on the phase branch when done.

### Requirements

R6: `skills/verify-work/SKILL.md` describes the enforced behavior and drops the claim that the engine does not enforce red-first.

### Design invariants

- Pass-only `tdd` + `done` + no finding → refuse.
- Valid red→green pair or finding escape → other close rules still apply.
- `check`/`manual` entries do not require `red_check_run_id`.
- Close never invents binary pass/fail for runner methods.

### Design assumptions

- Git available when both revisions are SHAs.
- verify-work can list check-runs for a criterion and pick the red to pass into the request.
- Runner-produced records remain distinguishable (e.g. `runner=se-workflow`) so hand-authored reds are refused.

### Decisions

- red-first-gate-locus: close-batch-refusal
- red-first-evidence-shape: request-carried
- red-first-ordering: git-ancestry
